gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-company acquisition where SCANA became a wholly owned subsidiary of Dominion Energy. The product/asset (T4), processes (T5), and organization/people (T6) all transferred together, with explicit contractual commitments to maintain the headquarters and employee compensation/benefits. There is no evidence of a structural mismatch between the product and its processes, or between the processes and the organization.

grok.rationale: The structural summary and closing 8-K state a whole-company reverse triangular merger in which SCANA (including SCE&G) survived as a wholly owned Dominion subsidiary, with legal vehicle, regulated utility product/asset, and people/management substrate all moving together. Merger Agreement Sections 5.06/5.16 contractually locked employee compensation, benefits, headquarters location, and continuity through 2019, so T4 product and T5 processes crossed aligned with T6 organization; no product-vs-process or process-vs-organization structural mismatch is documented at closing.

openai.rationale: The slice states that the whole company, including SCE&G's regulated utility products/assets and operations, transferred together rather than through a carve-out, so no product-process mismatch is documented at closing [SEC accession 0001193125-18-193204, DEFM14A, "The Merger Agreement" and structural summary]. It also documents contractual employee, benefits, union-term, headquarters, and management-continuity provisions accompanying those operations, so no process-organization mismatch is documented [SEC accession 0001193125-18-193204, DEFM14A Annex A, "Employee Matters" and "Additional Matters"].
